title: AI Movie Trailer Generator: How to Cut One in Four Beats
summary: An AI movie trailer generator renders whatever shots you ask for. Structure is the part it cannot do. Here is how to cut hook, build, turn and title card.
body_markdown:
## Article Highlights


- An AI movie trailer generator renders shots, not order
- Four beats: hook, build, turn, title card
- Write the turn first, then cut backwards to the hook
- Cut an AI movie trailer generator's shots to the music
- MPA rules give the Trailer Tag five seconds on screen
- Argil storyboards every shot before anything renders


An AI movie trailer generator turns a shot list into cut footage in minutes. A trailer still needs four beats to work. A hook, a build, a turn, a title card. The step most people botch is generating shots before they decide that order, then editing around footage they are stuck with.


## What an AI movie trailer generator does, and what it leaves to you


Rendering is the part[AI movie generators](https://www.argil.ai/blog/movie-generator) have gotten good at. A current tool will build frames from a description, hold a character's face across several shots, stitch the clips, and lay music underneath. None of that chooses which shot opens the trailer or how long it sits on screen.


Two of the articles ranking for this term today walk you through an interface. LTX Studio's steps run from defining the settings to editing your frames and exporting. ElevenLabs runs describe your vision, select a model, generate and save. Both are accurate about their own products, and neither mentions trailer structure anywhere, which is the part that decides whether anyone watches to the end.


## Step 1. Decide the four beats before you generate a frame


The hook is the first five to eight seconds of the trailer and its only job is to plant a question. A door that should not be open. One line of dialogue out of context. It explains nothing.


The build is the longest stretch. It shows the world, puts someone in trouble, and raises what the trouble costs them. Shots get shorter as the build runs, which is what makes a trailer feel like it is accelerating.


The turn is a single reveal that pays off the hook. One image, one line, or one cut that reframes what the build just set up.


Then the title card. The name, the date, nothing else.


Write the turn first and cut backwards to the hook. The turn is the only beat you cannot substitute, so every shot upstream exists to set it up. People who build forward from the hook tend to arrive at a turn they already spent, because the best image went into the first eight seconds where it had nothing to pay off.


No AI movie trailer generator decides that order for you. Argil is built around it. You bring an idea, shape the world, the characters, and the visual style, then direct the film shot by shot as a storyboard before anything renders. Argil's thesis states the division of labor this way.[The human is the director and AI is the crew](https://www.argil.ai/thesis) . The mechanic runs idea, storyboard, iteration, film. Pro starts at[$50 a month](https://www.argil.ai/) and the done-with-you Studio tier runs $1,250 a month, read from Argil's own homepage on October 20, 2026. If that is how you want to work,[that is where to start](https://www.argil.ai/?auth=signup) .


## Step 2. Pace the trailer against a clock


Pacing starts on paper. Take your shot list, which is what[a script turns into once it is broken down](https://www.argil.ai/blog/can-ai-write-a-movie-script-from-an-idea-in-2026) , and give every shot a duration before you render.


A 75 second trailer is roughly 18 to 22 shots. The worked example on Argil's homepage is a 30 second film built from 7 shots at 1080p, which averages a little over four seconds a shot. That average holds at trailer length.


Hold the hook longer than feels comfortable. Six seconds on one image is a long time on a feed. Cut tighter through the build, down to a second or less by the end of it. Give the turn the second longest hold in the piece. Three to five seconds on the title card, then stop.


An AI movie trailer with every shot held at an identical four seconds plays as a slideshow with music over the top.


## Step 3. Let the music set the cut, and keep the text short


Pick the track before you cut anything. Music is the pacing instrument, and cutting on its beats is what separates a trailer that drives from clips that happen in sequence. Most trailers change track or drop out entirely at the turn, and the drop is what tells a viewer the reveal has arrived. Half a second of silence before the turn does the same work.


Clear the rights on whatever you pick, or your AI movie trailer is locked to a track you cannot publish.[AI music tools](https://www.argil.ai/blog/suno-ai-alternatives-for-music-generation-how-to-create-music-videos-with-ai-2025) are the cheap route to a track you hold the rights to outright.


Text cards carry the exposition dialogue cannot fit into 75 seconds. Six words or fewer per card, and four cards across the whole trailer is plenty.


Two real constraints apply the moment a trailer plays in a cinema. The[MPA's Advertising Administration Rules](https://www.filmratings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/MPA-Advertising-Handbook-2025.pdf) , effective August 4, 2025, require the Trailer Tag to be displayed for five seconds, so your end card budget is fixed before you design it. The[Trailer Audio Standards Association](https://www.tasatrailers.org/) holds trailer loudness to an upper limit of Leq m 85, which sits well under the instinct to push everything loud.


## Where AI movie trailers fall apart


Character drift is the failure viewers notice in an AI movie trailer without being able to name it. A protagonist's face shifts between shot four and shot nine and the trailer stops reading as one film. Lock your character and style references before you generate, because regenerating one shot to match its neighbors usually moves both.


The other common failure is a trailer that is all build. It escalates for 70 seconds, shows a great deal, and never pays off the question the hook opened with. That happens when nobody decided the turn, so the edit simply runs out.


## FAQ


### How long should a movie trailer be?


No rule imposes a length. The MPA's current Advertising Administration Rules, effective August 4, 2025, set no maximum running time for a theatrical trailer, and the two minutes thirty seconds figure repeated across the internet does not appear in them. For a trailer that lives on a feed rather than in front of a feature, 60 to 90 seconds is the working range. Past 90 seconds you are asking for attention the hook has not earned yet.


### How do you make a movie trailer?


Decide the four beats, then generate. The hook plants a question in the first five to eight seconds. The build shows the world and the stakes, with shots that shorten as it runs. The turn is one reveal that pays off the hook. The title card gives the name and the date. Write the turn first and cut backwards from it.


### Can I make an AI movie trailer for free?


LTX Studio and ElevenLabs both advertise a free tier, which is enough to test a beat before you commit. Argil's cheapest paid plan starts at $50 a month, and plan credits refresh each month without stacking. A trailer you intend to publish is a paid job, so budget for it.
